## Chapter 1 — Doing, and being done to

*Doing, and being done to*

7 lessons · 33 words · 30 phrases

### 196. Something was done to it, the easy half

**Lesson 1 of 7** · Doing, and being done to
**Can do:** Read and build a passive sentence for ichidan verbs, する and 来る, and tell it apart from what being able to already sounds like
**Grammar:** `～られる` — Something was done to it. Ichidan verbs drop る and add られる; する becomes される, 来る becomes 来られる, read こられる. The same string the potential already uses -- context sorts them.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 見る | みる | to see, to watch |
| 食べる | たべる | to eat |
| する | する | to do |
| 来る | くる | to come |

- 彼はケーキをつまみ食いするのを見られた。 — He was seen eating a piece of the cake in secret.
- この回線の細さじゃ、動画は見られないよ。 — This connection is too slow for me to watch videos.
- 彼らの結婚式に招待された。 — I was invited to their wedding.
- 故人をしのんで、記念碑が建てられた。 — A monument was erected in memory of the deceased.

### 197. Something was done to it, the rest

**Lesson 2 of 7** · Doing, and being done to
**Can do:** Read and build a passive sentence for any verb
**Grammar:** `～れる` — The same thing for godan verbs -- move the last sound to the あ row and add れる. 書かれる, 話される, 呼ばれる, 読まれる, 買われる. う bends to わ; a verb ending in る may be either class, and the godan ones -- 帰る, 作る -- take this rule.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 書く | かく | to write |
| 泳ぐ | およぐ | to swim |
| 話す | はなす | to speak, to talk |
| 待つ | まつ | to wait |
| 死ぬ | しぬ | to die |
| 呼ぶ | よぶ | to call, to summon |
| 読む | よむ | to read |
| 買う | かう | to buy |
| 帰る | かえる | to return home |
| 作る | つくる | to make |
| 使う | つかう | to use |
| 英語 | えいご | English (language) |
| 花 | はな | flower |

- 校長室で会議が開かれた。 — The meeting was held in the principal's office.
- 英語はカナダで話されている。 — English is spoken in Canada.
- バラは花の女王と呼ばれている。 — The rose is called the queen of flowers.
- そのパーティーはいつ行われますか。 — When will the party be held?
- このワインは葡萄から作られています。 — This wine is made from grapes.

### 198. Who did it, and who it happened to

**Lesson 3 of 7** · Doing, and being done to
**Can do:** Build a full passive sentence — say what happened to something, and who did it, if it matters
**Grammar:** `～に～られる` — The full sentence. What was the object becomes the subject; whoever did it, if it is worth naming at all, takes に.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 姉 | あね | my older sister |
| 緑 | みどり | green |

- ママに叱られますよ。 — You'll get told off by Mum.
- 彼女はみんなに愛されている。 — She is loved by everybody.
- 彼は男まさりの姉に育てられた。 — He was brought up by his strong-willed sister.
- 湖は緑の丘に囲まれている。 — The lake is surrounded by green hills.

### 199. When it happens to you

**Lesson 4 of 7** · Doing, and being done to
**Can do:** Say that something happened to you — something taken, lost, or done around you — the way Japanese says it and English cannot
**Grammar:** `～を～れる` — It happened to you. The object keeps を and the person it happened to becomes the subject -- 財布を盗まれた. With a verb that has no object, 雨に降られた, there is nothing to keep.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 財布 | さいふ | wallet, purse |
| 車 | くるま | car |
| 雨 | あめ | rain |
| 死ぬ | しぬ | to die |
| わたし | わたし | I, me |

- 私は更衣室で財布を盗まれた。 — I had my wallet stolen in the changing room.
- 彼は真っ昼間に車を盗まれた。 — He had his car stolen in broad daylight.
- 雨に降られてぬれちゃったよ。 — I was caught in the rain and got wet.
- 私はガンで一人息子に死なれた。 — I had my only son die of cancer.

### 200. Making someone, letting someone

**Lesson 5 of 7** · Doing, and being done to
**Can do:** Say that you made or let someone do something, and ask politely to be allowed to do something yourself
**Grammar:** `～させる` — Making or letting someone do it. Godan verbs take あ row plus せる, ichidan verbs drop る and add させる. A causee taken from a transitive verb takes に, one taken from an intransitive verb usually takes を.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 待つ | まつ | to wait |
| 部屋 | へや | room |
| する | する | to do |
| 約束 | やくそく | arrangement, plans with someone |
| 人 | ひと | person, people |

- 彼は家政婦に部屋を掃除させた。 — He had the maid clean the room.
- コメディは人を笑わせるものである。 — Comedy is something that makes people laugh.
- 待たせてごめん。 — Sorry to have kept you waiting.
- 恐縮ですが、２月２７日の約束をキャンセルさせてください。 — I'm very sorry, but please let me cancel our appointment on the 27th of February.
- 相席させていただいてよろしいですか。 — May I share this table with you?

### 201. Made to do it

**Lesson 6 of 7** · Doing, and being done to
**Can do:** Say that you were made to do something, and recognise the colloquial contracted form when you meet it
**Grammar:** `～させられる` — Made to do it -- causative, then passive, stacked in that order. Godan verbs not ending in す contract in speech, and 待たせられた becomes 待たされた.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 待つ | まつ | to wait |
| する | する | to do |

- 上司に残業させられたんだよ。 — My boss made me work overtime.
- 彼は、自分の意志に反して契約書に署名させられた。 — He was made to sign the contract against his will.
- 彼に１時間待たされた。 — He kept me waiting for an hour.
- 私たちは一列に並ばされた。 — We were made to stand in a line.

### 202. By, this time for real

**Lesson 7 of 7** · Doing, and being done to
**Can do:** Say who or what did something, in the formal register
**Grammar:** `～によって～れる` — By, in the formal register -- によって (written により) naming the agent of a passive sentence. Its other two jobs, means and variation, come in the next chapter.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 音楽 | おんがく | music |
| 弟 | おとうと | my younger brother |

- この音楽はバッハによって作曲された。 — This music was composed by Bach.
- 紙は中国人によって発明された。 — Paper was invented by the Chinese.
- サッカーのチームはトムによって引率される。 — The soccer team is led by Tom.
- 一番下の弟は祖母により幼年時代育てられた。 — My youngest brother was brought up by our grandmother.

### 203. Recognition checkpoint — closes the chapter

> A wide pass over everything this chapter has taught. Type the reading or the meaning rather than picking it out of a line-up. One ending built two ways, one auxiliary stacked on another, and one formal marker for the person behind it all. What is being checked is not whether you can recite a table — it is whether the right reading comes to hand for the sentence in front of you. Some of what comes back is a られる sentence that could be about being able to or could be about something that happened, and the only way through it is to read the rest of the sentence. That is the skill this chapter exists to build, so it is the one worth checking. The を that stays put when a wallet is stolen is worth watching for, and so is the difference between a contraction and a verb that only looks like one. Anything you miss comes back sooner. It finishes when the remaining set empties; retry as often as you like, nothing is recorded.

## Chapter 2 — Cause and consequence

*Cause and consequence*

7 lessons · 24 words · 29 phrases

### 204. Because, and in order to

**Lesson 1 of 7** · Cause and consequence
**Can do:** Explain what something is for, and what caused it
**Grammar:** `～ために` — In order to, and because of. A dictionary-form verb in front usually means purpose; a noun plus の, or a past clause, usually means cause. ため on its own is an ordinary noun meaning benefit, which is where ためになる comes from.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 家 | いえ | house, home |
| 帰る | かえる | to return home |
| 見る | みる | to see, to watch |
| 子供 | こども | child, children |
| 雨 | あめ | rain |
| 全部 | ぜんぶ | all, everything |

- 着替えをするために家に帰った。 — I went home to change my clothes.
- 私達みんなは芝居を見るためにシアターへ行った。 — All of us went to the theater to see a play.
- 彼女は子供のために全てを犠牲にした。 — She gave up everything for her children.
- 大雨のためにダムが決壊した。 — The dam burst owing to the heavy rain.
- 霧のために、交通は一時不通になっている。 — Due to the fog, traffic is temporarily suspended.
- 日常の運動はあなたのためになる。 — Everyday exercise is good for you.

### 205. Whose fault it is

**Lesson 2 of 7** · Cause and consequence
**Can do:** Blame something for how things turned out
**Grammar:** `～せいで` — Because of, and it turned out badly. Noun plus の, or any plain clause, in front. せいだ ends the sentence instead of joining two; せいか hedges it to maybe because of.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 頭 | あたま | head |
| 雨 | あめ | rain |
| 飛行機 | ひこうき | aeroplane |

- 気のせいだよ。 — It's just your imagination.
- あなたの頭痛は過労のせいだ。 — Your headache comes from overwork.
- 彼は勉強不足のせいで試験に落ちました。 — He failed the exam because he had not studied enough.
- 雨が降らなかったせいで草木が枯れてしまった。 — The plants died because it didn't rain.
- 飛行機でお酒飲むと、気圧のせいか酔いやすい。 — Maybe it's the air pressure, but you get drunk more easily on a plane.

### 206. Who gets the credit

**Lesson 3 of 7** · Cause and consequence
**Can do:** Give something the credit for how things turned out
**Grammar:** `～おかげで` — Thanks to, and it turned out well. Same shape as せいで, opposite stance. おかげである or おかげです ends the sentence; おかげさまで is a fixed thank-you of its own.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 仕事 | しごと | work, job |
| 両親 | りょうしん | parents, both parents |
| 痛い | いたい | painful, sore |

- あなたのおかげで仕事がうまく行きました。 — Thanks to you, the job went well.
- 私はあなたの援助のおかげで成功した。 — I succeeded thanks to your help.
- 錠剤のおかげで痛みがなくなった。 — Thanks to the tablets, the pain went away.
- 私が今日あるのは両親のおかげである。 — I owe what I am to my parents.
- そのおかげで誤解が解ける。 — Thanks to that, misunderstandings are cleared up.

### 207. By, and according to

**Lesson 4 of 7** · Cause and consequence
**Can do:** Say what a difference comes from — a method, or a rule that things vary by
**Grammar:** `～によって` — By this means, or varying with this. Noun plus によって, or a clause plus こと plus によって. により is the same word in a more written register. Marking the agent of a passive sentence is its third job and belongs to the previous chapter.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 本 | ほん | book |
| 読む | よむ | to read |
| こと | こと | thing, matter |
| 国 | くに | country |
| お金 | おかね | money |
| 地図 | ちず | map |

- 私は本を読むことによって知識を得る。 — I get knowledge by reading books.
- 私達は経験によって多くを学ぶ。 — We learn much by experience.
- テーブルマナーは国によって異なる。 — Table manners vary from one country to another.
- 人の生活様式の大半はお金によって決まる。 — One's lifestyle is largely determined by money.
- ご要望により地図を送ります。 — We will send you a map on request.

### 208. Now that

**Lesson 5 of 7** · Cause and consequence
**Can do:** Say what follows, now that something is already true
**Grammar:** `～からには` — Now that this is settled, here is what follows. Plain form plus からには, and the second half usually carries resolve, obligation or a command rather than a plain fact.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 困る | こまる | to be in trouble, to be stuck |
| 時間 | じかん | time, hour |

- いやしくもやるからには上手くやれ。 — If you do it at all, do it well.
- 私の参謀としてついたからには、危機感を持って任にあたって貰わねば困ります。 — If you're with me as a staff officer, then I need you to bring a sense of danger with you to your work.
- 海戦に先立って出港したからには、乗組員が船に慣れる時間がないことが、しばしばあるものだ。 — A sailor frequently has no time to get his sea legs after leaving port before a battle starts.

### 209. Explaining yourself

**Lesson 6 of 7** · Cause and consequence
**Can do:** Explain why you did what you did, the way you would explain it to a friend
**Grammar:** `～ものだから` — That is why, you see. A plain clause plus ものだから, excusing or accounting for something rather than just reporting it. もんだから in speech.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| こと | こと | thing, matter |
| 書く | かく | to write |
| 母 | はは | my mother |

- ええ、このところ野宿ばかりだったものだから、久しぶりにゆっくり出来ました。ありがとう。 — Yes, thanks. Recently I've been roughing it so I was able to get a proper sleep for the first time in a while.
- いつも妙ちくりんなことばっかり書いてるもんだから、きっとコメントしにくいんだわ！ — I'm always writing weird stuff, so I'm sure it's hard to comment on.
- この金時計は私にとって非常に大切なものだ。母が晩年に形見として私にくれたものだから。 — This gold watch means a great deal to me. It's because my mother gave it to me as a keepsake in her later years.

### 210. Knowing them

**Lesson 7 of 7** · Cause and consequence
**Can do:** Predict what someone will do, because you know them
**Grammar:** `～ことだから` — Knowing them, this follows. A person plus の plus ことだから predicts from character, so what comes after is a guess. A past clause plus ことだから is the plainer since it is the case that.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| こと | こと | thing, matter |

- あなたのことだから上々でしょう。 — Knowing you, I'm sure it went splendidly.
- 自分でやったことだから仕方がないね。 — You did it to yourself, so there's nothing to be done.

### 211. Recognition checkpoint — closes the chapter

> A wide pass over everything this chapter has taught. Type the reading or the meaning rather than picking it out of a line-up. Five words for because, plus によって and からには, and the work is not remembering their shapes but knowing which one a sentence has reached for and why. What is being checked is the choice. せいで and おかげで are the same grammar pointing opposite ways, and getting them the wrong way round says the opposite of what you meant, so those two are worth the most attention when they come back. ため's two readings are the other thing to watch: nothing in the form separates purpose from cause, and the sentence around it does. によって comes back too, and it now has three jobs across two chapters — one of them is the previous chapter's and it is fair game here. Some of what returns is a familiar sentence rather than a new one. For からには, ものだから and ことだから that is deliberate: there are three, four and two of these sentences in existence, and reusing one you have seen is a smaller cost than inventing one, which this book will not do. Recognising what a word is doing in a sentence you have met before is still the thing being asked. Anything you miss comes back sooner. It finishes when the remaining set empties; retry as often as you like, nothing is recorded.

## Chapter 3 — Even though

*Even though*

6 lessons · 15 words · 27 phrases

### 212. Even though, plainly

**Lesson 1 of 6** · Even though
**Can do:** React to something that contradicts what you would have expected
**Grammar:** `～のに` — Even though. Straight onto a plain verb or い-adjective; a noun or な-adjective takes な first -- 学生なのに. On its own at the end of a sentence it is a complaint with the rest left unsaid.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 両親 | りょうしん | parents, both parents |
| 立つ | たつ | to stand up |
| 着る | きる | to wear, to put on (upper body) |

- 空席があるのに立っていてもしょうがない。 — There is no sense in standing when there are seats available.
- あんなに長所が多いのに彼女は誇らなかった。 — Even though she had so many good points, she was not proud.
- 彼は３８歳なのに両親に頼りきりです。 — Though 38, he is still dependent on his parents.
- もっと一生懸命勉強すべきだったのに。 — You should have studied harder.
- 夏服を着ればいいのに。 — Why don't you wear summer clothes?
- それを建てるのに何年もかかった。 — It took many years to build it.

### 213. Even though, with an edge

**Lesson 2 of 6** · Even though
**Can do:** Point out a contradiction with an edge of criticism to it
**Grammar:** `～くせに` — Even though, with a sneer. Same attachment as のに on a verb or い-adjective, but a noun takes の rather than な -- 新米のくせに. Never neutral; it always blames.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 太い | ふとい | thick, wide |
| 細い | ほそい | thin, narrow |
| 言う | いう | to say |

- 彼は太っているくせに声は細い。 — His voice is thin even though he is fat.
- 新米のくせに大きな顔をするな。 — Don't act so big when you are the new one here.
- 青二才のくせに何を言うか。 — That's big talk for an upstart like you.
- 最近は、年下のくせにため口を聞く奴が多すぎる。 — These days there are far too many people who talk to you as an equal even though they are younger.

### 214. The other job of ながら

**Lesson 3 of 6** · Even though
**Can do:** Recognise and produce even though using a form you already own for something else
**Grammar:** `～ながらも` — Even though, from the ながら you already have. The も marks the concessive sense unmistakably; without it the same ending is usually while, and only the sentence around it decides.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 女 | おんな | woman |
| 走る | はしる | to run |
| 言う | いう | to say |

- 彼女は不本意ながらもそうした。 — She did it against her will.
- 女ながらも彼女は勇敢だった。 — Even though she was a woman, she was brave.
- ぜいぜい言いながらも、気合をいれて走り続ける。 — Even though we were wheezing, we kept running with renewed vigour.
- あれほど金を持ちながら彼は幸福でない。 — For all his wealth, he is not happy.
- その悪い知らせは残念ながら本当だ。 — The bad news is unfortunately true.

### 215. Although, in writing

**Lesson 4 of 6** · Even though
**Can do:** Read a formal although joining two clauses, and use it in writing of your own
**Grammar:** `～ものの` — Although, in writing. Onto a plain predicate, けど's meaning in an essay's register. Most ものの in real text is もの plus の instead, so read the sentence, not the string.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 会社 | かいしゃ | company, office |
| 行く | いく | to go |

- パーティーに行くことにしたものの、気が進まない。 — Though I have decided to go to the party, I'm not looking forward to it.
- 汚い手で会社を乗っ取ったものの、腹心だと思っていた部下に裏切られ、因果応報だね。 — He took the company over by dirty means, but was betrayed by the subordinate he thought was his right hand -- what goes around comes around.
- 高校時代からつきあっている彼氏はいるものの、つきあいが惰性になっていると感じ、不満をつのらせている。 — She has a boyfriend she's been going out with since high school but feels their relationship has become a matter of habit and is increasingly dissatisfied.
- 東洋人はものの見方が我々とは違う。 — People from the East do not look at things the same as we do.

### 216. That said

**Lesson 5 of 6** · Even though
**Can do:** Recognise a formal that said or granted that, and tell it from the phrase it looks like
**Grammar:** `～とはいえ` — That said. Granting a point and overruling it, onto a noun with no copula or onto a plain predicate. Not とは言えない, which is 言う in the potential negative.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 若い | わかい | young |
| 言う | いう | to say |

- あぁ……、若かったとはいえ、しょうもない凡ミスだ。 — Ahh... I was young, but what a stupid careless mistake.
- 流言飛語に惑わされるべからず、とはいうものの、言うは易く行うは難し、と思わない？ — They say you shouldn't be taken in by rumours, but that's easier said than done, don't you think?
- あなたの考えはとても実際的とはいえない。 — Your ideas are hardly practical.

### 217. Despite that

**Lesson 6 of 6** · Even though
**Can do:** Read and use despite and regardless of in formal writing
**Grammar:** `～にもかかわらず` — Despite. Onto a bare noun or a plain clause, and standing alone as それにもかかわらず. Drop the も and にかかわらず means regardless of instead.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 疲れる | つかれる | to get tired |
| 晴れ | はれ | sunny, clear (weather) |

- 晴天にもかかわらず、空気は冷え冷えとしていた。 — In spite of the sunny weather, the air was rather chilly.
- 彼の努力にもかかわらず、すべては以前と変りなかった。 — Despite his efforts, nothing was any different from before.
- 芳男は反証があるにもかかわらず、そう信じ続けた。 — Yoshio went on believing it, despite the evidence to the contrary.
- 私は疲れていたが、それにもかかわらず眠れなかった。 — I was tired, but even so I could not sleep.
- マラソンは晴雨にかかわらず開かれます。 — The marathon will be held, rain or shine.

### 218. Recognition checkpoint — closes the chapter

> A wide pass over everything this chapter has taught. Type the reading or the meaning rather than picking it out of a line-up. Six ways of saying even though, and the work is not remembering that they exist — it is knowing which one a sentence is using and whether it is using one at all. Half of what comes back is a look-alike: のに that means for the purpose of, ものの that is just a thing and its, とはいえない that is a verb in the negative, にかかわらず that means regardless rather than despite. Reading past those is the skill this chapter was built to give you, so it is the one worth checking. The noun row is worth watching for too — な in front of のに, の in front of くせに — and so is the も that tells ながら's two jobs apart. Anything you miss comes back sooner. It finishes when the remaining set empties; retry as often as you like, nothing is recorded.

## Chapter 4 — Conditions, sharpened

*Conditions, sharpened*

7 lessons · 38 words · 42 phrases

### 219. As long as it holds

**Lesson 1 of 7** · Conditions, sharpened
**Can do:** Say that something stays true for exactly as long as something else does, and say its flip side, unless
**Grammar:** `～限り` — For as long as it holds. Plain non-past, ている or plain negative, then 限り -- no conjugation of its own. Negated, ない限り, English says either "as long as you don't" or "unless".

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| ある | ある | to exist, to have (inanimate) |
| いる | いる | to exist, to be (animate) |
| 忘れる | わすれる | to forget, to leave behind |
| 本 | ほん | book |

- 命がある限りあなたのご恩は忘れません。 — As long as I live, I will never forget your kindness.
- 我々は生きている限り学び続けなければならない。 — We must continue to study as long as we live.
- 飲み食いするものが十分ある限り彼は何も気にしない。 — He doesn't care, provided he has enough to eat and drink.
- 汚さない限り、この本を持ち帰ってもいいですよ。 — You may take this book as long as you keep it clean.
- もっと勉強しない限り落第しますよ。 — You will fail unless you work harder.

### 220. As far as I know

**Lesson 2 of 7** · Conditions, sharpened
**Can do:** Limit what you are claiming to what you know, what you can see, or what you can manage
**Grammar:** `～限りでは` — Within the limit of. 限り is a noun meaning a limit, and 知る限り, 見渡す限り and できる限り all say "as far as" -- as far as I know, as far as the eye reaches, as far as I am able. では is common and optional.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 知る | しる | to know |
| 見る | みる | to see, to watch |
| 海 | うみ | sea, ocean |
| できる | できる | to be able to, to be good at |
| 高い | たかい | expensive, tall, high |

- 宇宙には限りはない。 — There is no limit to the universe.
- 私の知る限りでは彼は正直です。 — As far as I know, he is honest.
- 見渡す限り海だった。 — There was nothing but the ocean as far as the eye could see.
- 私はできる限りあなたの援助をします。 — I'll help you as much as I can.
- 肩書きが偉くても地位が高いとは限らない。 — A big title does not necessarily mean a high position.

### 221. If only you'd just

**Lesson 3 of 7** · Conditions, sharpened
**Can do:** Say that one thing on its own is enough to settle the matter
**Grammar:** `～さえ～ば` — This one thing and nothing else is enough. さえ means "even", and in front of a ば you already build it narrows the condition to a minimum -- ます-stem plus さえ plus すれば, or a noun plus さえ with the verb itself in ば.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 押す | おす | to push, to press |
| 走る | はしる | to run |
| 車 | くるま | car |
| 覚える | おぼえる | to memorise, to remember |
| 会う | あう | to meet |
| 雨 | あめ | rain |

- あなたはボタンを押しさえすればいい。 — All you have to do is press the button.
- 走りさえすれば、どんな車でもよいのです。 — Any car will do, as long as it runs.
- コツさえ覚えれば、朝飯前ですよ。 — Once you get the hang of it, it's easy.
- 彼に会う機会さえあればなあ。 — If only I get a chance to see him.
- 雨がやみさえすればいいのになあ。 — If only it would stop raining!

### 222. Two ways to say "as long as"

**Lesson 4 of 7** · Conditions, sharpened
**Can do:** Choose between 限り and さえ〜ば when English says "as long as", and say what each of them is actually claiming

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| ある | ある | to exist, to have (inanimate) |
| 走る | はしる | to run |
| 車 | くるま | car |
| いる | いる | to exist, to be (animate) |

- 飲み食いするものが十分ある限り彼は何も気にしない。 — He doesn't care, provided he has enough to eat and drink.
- 走りさえすれば、どんな車でもよいのです。 — Any car will do, as long as it runs.
- 命がある限りあなたのご恩は忘れません。 — As long as I live, I will never forget your kindness.
- あなたはボタンを押しさえすればいい。 — All you have to do is press the button.

### 223. Depends on it, or the moment it's done

**Lesson 5 of 7** · Conditions, sharpened
**Can do:** Say that one thing depends on another, and that something will happen the moment something else is finished
**Grammar:** `～次第` — It depends on that. A bare noun plus 次第, no particle and no copula between them. On a ます-stem the same word means the moment something is done -- 着き次第, as soon as I arrive. Watch for 次第に, the adverb "gradually", which is neither.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 仕事 | しごと | work, job |
| 天気 | てんき | weather |
| 着く | つく | to arrive |
| 電話 | でんわ | telephone |
| する | する | to do |

- 選択は全く君次第だ。 — The choice is all up to you.
- 仕事の成功はあなた方の努力次第です。 — Our success in this work depends on your efforts.
- ビアガーデンに客がたくさんいるかどうかは天気次第だ。 — Whether or not beer gardens get a lot of customers depends on the weather.
- 空港に着き次第、電話します。 — I'll phone you as soon as I get to the airport.
- あなたの用意が出来次第出発しましょう。 — We'll leave as soon as you are ready.
- その急行列車は次第に速度を上げた。 — The express train picked up speed gradually.

### 224. Even if it doesn't go your way

**Lesson 6 of 7** · Conditions, sharpened
**Can do:** Say that something holds no matter what happens, including the worst case
**Grammar:** `たとえ～ても` — Even if -- the outcome holds regardless. te-form plus も for verbs, くても for い-adjectives, でも for な-adjectives and nouns, なくても for negatives. たとえ in front is emphasis and can be left out.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 雨 | あめ | rain |
| 高い | たかい | expensive, tall, high |
| 古い | ふるい | old (for things, not people) |
| 買う | かう | to buy |
| 今 | いま | now |
| 来る | くる | to come |
| 困る | こまる | to be in trouble, to be stuck |

- たとえ雨が降っても、その試合は行われるだろう。 — The game will be played even if it rains.
- たとえ多忙でも彼は来るだろう。 — Even if he is busy, he will come.
- たとえ困っていても、マックはいつも楽天的だ。 — Even if he is in trouble, Mac is always optimistic.
- どんなに高くても、あの古い時計を買います。 — I'll buy that old clock, however expensive it is.
- 今はそうじゃなくても将来はいい夫になるよ。 — Even if he isn't now, he'll be a good husband in the future.
- たとえどんなことがあってもあきらめません。 — No matter what happens, I won't give up.

### 225. Every "if" at once

**Lesson 7 of 7** · Conditions, sharpened
**Can do:** Pick the conditional a Japanese speaker would actually use, out of everything you now have

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 時間 | じかん | time, hour |
| 行く | いく | to go |
| 会う | あう | to meet |
| 使う | つかう | to use |
| 走る | はしる | to run |
| 押す | おす | to push, to press |
| ある | ある | to exist, to have (inanimate) |

- あの政治家に会うつもりなら、袖の下を使わない限り駄目だね。 — That politician won't meet you unless you grease his palm.
- 世界最速の走者でさえ、空腹だったら走れない。 — Even the fastest runner in the world cannot run if he is hungry.
- 命がある限りあなたのご恩は忘れません。 — As long as I live, I will never forget your kindness.
- あなたはボタンを押しさえすればいい。 — All you have to do is press the button.
- たとえ雨が降っても、その試合は行われるだろう。 — The game will be played even if it rains.
- 選択は全く君次第だ。 — The choice is all up to you.
- 時間があったら、行きます。 — If I have time, I'll go.
- 押すと、開きます。 — Press it, and it opens.
- 高ければ、買いません。 — If it's expensive, I won't buy it.
- 雨なら、タクシーで行きます。 — If it's raining, I'll go by taxi.
- 疲れたら、休んだほうがいいです。 — If you're tired, you should rest.

### 226. Recognition checkpoint — closes the chapter

> A wide pass over everything this chapter has taught. Type the reading or the meaning rather than picking it out of a line-up. Four connectives, two of them doing two jobs and one of them a particle you had never met, and what is being checked is not whether you can recite a table — it is whether the right reading comes to hand for the sentence in front of you. Some of what comes back is a 限り that bounds a promise and some is a 限り that hedges a claim, and the only way through is to read the rest of the sentence. Same for 次第 against 次第に, and for a さえ with a ば after it against a さえ with nothing after it at all. Those are the collisions this chapter exists to sort out, so they are the ones worth checking. Anything you miss comes back sooner. It finishes when the remaining set empties; retry as often as you like, nothing is recorded.

## Chapter 5 — More than one way to say "when"

*More than one way to say "when"*

7 lessons · 29 words · 30 phrases

### 227. Before it's too late

**Lesson 1 of 7** · More than one way to say "when"
**Can do:** Say to do something now, while a passing state or chance is still true
**Grammar:** `～うちに` — While it is still true -- and it will not be for long. Attaches like 時 does, straight onto a plain verb or an い-adjective. Very often negative, 〜ないうちに, which is how Japanese says before X happens.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 時 | とき | time, moment, occasion |
| 若い | わかい | young |
| 体 | からだ | body |
| 家 | いえ | house, home |

- スープは熱いうちに召し上がって下さい。 — Eat your soup while it is hot.
- 若いうちに体を鍛えなさい。 — Build up your body while young.
- 私たちは暗くならないうちにテントを張った。 — We set up our tents before dark.
- 消防車が到着しないうちに、その家は丸焼けになった。 — Before the fire engine arrived, the whole house had burnt down.

### 228. Sometime while it lasts

**Lesson 2 of 7** · More than one way to say "when"
**Can do:** Say something happened at one point during a stretch of time, or lasted the whole of it
**Grammar:** `～間に` — During a stretch of time. With に, the second thing is a bounded event completed inside the stretch; without に, it runs the whole length. This is the 間 of vocab.aida doing a second job -- not the space between two things, a span of time.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 間 | あいだ | between |
| 時 | とき | time, moment, occasion |
| 電話 | でんわ | telephone |
| 洗う | あらう | to wash |

- ヨーロッパにいる間に僕はパリをたずねた。 — I visited Paris while I was in Europe.
- 彼女が電話をしている間にふろ桶があふれた。 — The tub ran over while she was on the phone.
- あなたが皿を洗っている間に、私は床を掃除します。 — I'll sweep the floor while you wash the dishes.
- ネクタイを締める間、ちょっとじっとしてね。 — Hold still a moment while I fix your tie.
- 毎朝朝食をとっている間、彼の犬は彼をじっと見つめていた。 — His dog stared at him every morning while he had his breakfast.

### 229. The formal way to say "when"

**Lesson 3 of 7** · More than one way to say "when"
**Can do:** Say "when" the way an announcement, an instruction or a rule does
**Grammar:** `～際に` — When, in the formal register -- signs, manuals, announcements, rules. Same attachment as 時 -- plain verb direct, noun with の. 際は rather than 際に when the clause sets up a case.
**New kanji:** 際

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 時 | とき | time, moment, occasion |
| 友達 | ともだち | friend |
| 電話 | でんわ | telephone |

- ドアを開ける際に、私は鍵を壊してしまった。 — When I opened the door, I broke the lock.
- 火事の際は１１９番に電話してください。 — In the case of fire, dial 119.
- 離陸の際は、シートベルトを締めなくてはならない。 — You must fasten your seat belts during take-off.
- 長野にいる友人を訪問した際、おいしいそばをごちそうになった。 — When I visited my friend in Nagano, I was treated to delicious soba.

### 230. The instant it happened

**Lesson 4 of 7** · More than one way to say "when"
**Can do:** Say one thing happened the very instant another did, and that nobody saw it coming
**Grammar:** `～たとたん` — The instant one thing happened, another did. Takes a plain past verb and nothing else -- no non-past, no adjective, no noun. The second half is usually something nobody saw coming. Written 途端 as well as とたん.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 時 | とき | time, moment, occasion |
| 聞く | きく | to listen, to ask |
| 開ける | あける | to open (something) |

- これをきいたとたん、彼は真っ青になった。 — On hearing this, he turned pale.
- ドアを開けたとたんに、彼は焦げ臭い匂いを嗅いだ。 — The instant he opened the door, he smelt something burning.
- その知らせを聞いたとたんに彼女は青くなった。 — The moment she heard the news, she turned pale.
- トムがテレビをつけたとたんにヒューズがとんだ。 — No sooner had Tom turned on the TV than the fuse blew.

### 231. Partway there

**Lesson 5 of 7** · More than one way to say "when"
**Can do:** Say something happened partway through a trip or a task that was not finished yet
**Grammar:** `～途中で` — Partway through something not yet finished -- a journey or a task. Plain verb direct, noun with の, or standing alone. Not a moment on a clock, but a place inside a process.
**New kanji:** 途

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 時 | とき | time, moment, occasion |
| 駅 | えき | station |
| 学校 | がっこう | school |
| 行く | いく | to go |
| 会う | あう | to meet |

- 駅へ行く途中でにわか雨に遭った。 — I was caught in a shower on my way to the station.
- 学校へ行く途中でトムに会った。 — I met Tom on my way to school.
- 途中であきらめるな。 — Don't give up halfway.
- 講義の途中で彼女は吐き気を催した。 — Halfway through the lecture, she began to feel sick.

### 232. Ever since

**Lesson 6 of 7** · More than one way to say "when"
**Can do:** Say something has been true continuously, starting from one clear point in the past
**Grammar:** `～以来` — Ever since a point in the past, and still. Straight onto a noun with no particle, or onto a te-form verb. The starting point has to be over already, and what follows has to still hold.
**New kanji:** 以

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 時 | とき | time, moment, occasion |
| 会う | あう | to meet |
| 飲む | のむ | to drink |
| 死ぬ | しぬ | to die |

- １９８８年以来トムに会っていません。 — I haven't seen Tom since 1988.
- 爆破予告以来、空港の警備体制は強化された。 — Security at the airport has been stepped up since the bomb scare.
- 彼は妻が死んで以来酒を飲む癖がついた。 — He has taken to drinking since the death of his wife.
- それ以来彼のうわさは聞いていない。 — He has never been heard of since.

### 233. Started, and then

**Lesson 7 of 7** · More than one way to say "when"
**Can do:** Say you started something and did not finish it, or that something was on the point of happening
**Grammar:** `～かける` — Started and not finished, or on the point of starting. An auxiliary on a verb's ます-stem, not a noun -- 言いかける, 死にかける. Conjugates as an ichidan verb, and freezes into a noun as 〜かけ.

| Word | Reading | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| かける | かける | to put on (glasses), to hang |
| 宿題 | しゅくだい | homework |
| 忘れる | わすれる | to forget, to leave behind |
| 顔 | かお | face |
| おばあさん | おばあさん | grandmother, elderly woman |
| 死ぬ | しぬ | to die |

- 宿題をやりかけにしておいた。 — I left my homework half-done.
- 彼が何か言いかけたが先手を打ってやった。 — He started to say something, but I beat him to it.
- 私はおばあさんの顔をもう忘れかけている。 — I am already forgetting my grandmother's face.
- その男は死にかけていた。 — The man was on the brink of death.
- 演奏は終わりかけていた。 — The performance was almost over.

### 234. Recognition checkpoint — closes the chapter

> A wide pass over everything this chapter has taught, and this is also where the seven get set side by side, since they were deliberately taught one at a time. 時 is still the neutral default and has not been demoted — it is correct far more often than not, and reaching for it is never an error of grammar. What the others add on top of it is the thing to have straight. うちに adds a deadline: the state in front of it is running out, and 〜ないうちに is how before happens is said. 間 adds a bounded stretch, and its one particle decides everything — に for a thing that happened at a point inside, no に for a thing that lasted the whole length. 際 adds register and nothing else, and only where there is an occasion to point at. たとたん adds an instant with no gap and a second half nobody saw coming, past tense, plain past verb in front, no exceptions to look up. Then two that are not competing for when at all, and that is the distinction most worth checking. 途中で puts you inside something unfinished — a journey short of its destination, a task short of its end. かける puts the incompleteness inside the verb itself: started and dropped, or not started and nearly there. Neither answers when something happened; they answer how far along it was. Type the reading or the meaning rather than picking it out of a line-up. Some of what comes back will hinge on one small thing — a に present or absent after 間, a negative in front of うちに that English throws away in translation, a かける that turns out to be 出かける and not this pattern at all. Those are the places worth slowing down. Anything you miss comes back sooner. It finishes when the remaining set empties; retry as often as you like, nothing is recorded.
